title: Aurum Alpha pinned base image reference
description: The grammar of a pinned base image (SB1 of standards/085-security-baseline.md): an OCI reference addressed by digest, with its human-readable version carried in-band as the tag or in a trailing comment. A checker applies these patterns to every FROM line in every Dockerfile, exempting only 'scratch', a reference to a stage the same file declared with AS, and the --platform flag. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

digest.description: An OCI content digest: the sha256 algorithm and 64 lowercase hex characters. Content-addressed and immutable by the OCI distribution specification, which is why it is the pin and a tag is not (SB1).

imageName.description: An OCI image name: optional registry host with optional port, then one or more lowercase path components. No tag, no digest (SB1).

tag.description: An OCI tag: the human-readable version the runtime ignores when a digest is present, kept because a digest alone cannot be reviewed (SB1).

pinnedReference.description: The canonical pinned reference: <name>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>. The tag is the version comment carried in-band, and an update tool maintains both halves as one edit (SB1).

pinnedFromLine.description:
A FROM line in either admitted form: the in-band form 'FROM [--platform=

] :@sha256: [AS ]', or the comment form 'FROM [--platform=

] @sha256: [AS ] # '. A digest with neither a tag nor a comment does not match, because it is a pin nobody can read (SB1). The instruction keyword is case-insensitive in a Dockerfile and the pattern admits both spellings.

finding.description: The findings SB1's checker reports, one per offending FROM line: tag_not_digest (no digest at all, an implicit latest included), digest_malformed (an @ reference that is not sha256 plus 64 hex), version_missing (a digest with neither tag nor comment), unreadable_reference (a build argument or other reference the checker cannot resolve without evaluating the build).
